text:
kai: Heads up — seeing a spike in GPU pod preemptions in us-west-2-gpu pool since ~10:10 UTC. A lot of inference pods getting preempted repeatedly.

devon: Yep, ~125 evictions in the last 35m. Scheduler logs show 'taint-based preemption' + tons of 'failed to allocate device' from device-plugin.

kai: Snippet of what I ran:```kubectl get events -n prod --field-selector reason=Preempted | tail -n 50``` shows repeated preemption for pods with priority=inference-high.

maria: Did we just roll the new taint 'gpu-evict=true:NoExecute' across that pool? I thought it was supposed to be for spot-only nodes.

devon: We did the rollout last night but a terraform var was undefined for the us-west-2-gpu module, so the taint ended up applied to all GPU nodes in that AZ accidentally.

aj: FWIW device-plugin v0.11 has a leak where allocations persist after kubelet restart; scheduler thinks GPUs are free, pod gets scheduled, then device-plugin errors and pod gets preempted. Could be interacting.

kai: Got device-plugin logs that match: "error: failed to allocate gpu-uuid abcde: allocation still referenced by pod prod/serve-xyz" — repeated during pod startup.

sre-bot: [autoscaler] Cluster Autoscaler scaled down 6 nodes in us-west-2-gpu at 10:05 UTC (reason: underutilized).

maria: Short-term plan: revert the taint rollout for the AZ, set explicit podPriority for inference-high so they don't get preempted by automation. Medium: pin device-plugin to v0.10 and roll. Long: add rollout guard to terraform and an integration test for taint application.

aj: I'll open an ops ticket and coordinate a fast device-plugin patch rollout + taint revert. Also will add a temporary descheduler job to evict low-priority pods from the GPU pool.

devon: Cost shout: retries bumped GPU runtime this hour — rough estimate +$1.2k extra. Put a note on the incident.

kai: Okay starting the rollback now, will post updates. :thumbsup:
